newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NBS CUTS MORTGAGE RATE TO 19 PCT FROM OCT 1.
newsitem.headline: NBS CUTS MORTGAGE RATE TO 19 PCT FROM OCT 1.

text.p: NBS Holdings Ltd announced on Thursday that it would cut its base rate for home loans by 25 basis points to 19 percent with effect from October 1.
NBS mortgage lending general manager Trevor Olivier said the decrease was effective for existing loans from October 1 and immediately on new applications.
"The property market has been looking for a positive signal for improvement and it has finally arrived after many months of speculation," Olivier said.

Standard Bank Investment Corp on Wednesday announced a cut in its prime overdraft rate by 0.25 points to 19.25 percent. This move was on Thursday followed by similar 0.25 point reductions by First National Bank Holdings Ltd, Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Lts and Nedcor Ltd on Thursday. The banks' base home loan rate was also reduced by a similar amount to 19 percent.

The banks said rate cuts reflected the government's decision to scrap the Financial Services Levy (FSL) and replace it with value added tax (VAT) on financial services from next month. FSL was first introduced by the South African government in 1991, when banks increased prime by 0.25 percent to recover the cost.
